title: PCPP property
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite alphabet, let $n\ge 1$, and let $V$ be a PCPP system with input length $n$, proof length $\ell$, and query count $r$. For a property $P$ of length-$n$ words over $\mathcal A$ and a real number $\rho$, suppose $\rho>0$. Every word $w$ satisfying $P$ has some proof that $V$ accepts with probability $1$; moreover, for every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, if every word satisfying $P$ is at distance at least $\varepsilon$ from $w$, then every proof is rejected on $w$ with probability strictly greater than $\rho\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: V is a PCPP system of input length n, proof length ℓ, and query count r
P is a property of length-n words
ρ is a real number and 0 < ρ
For every P-satisfying w, there exists a proof accepted with probability 1
Every P-satisfying word w' is at distance at least ε from w
